The 22nd FJ Division is here to support us, their mission is to take the Isle of Wight, however, you can change those plans if needed. Good Luck!

In the winter of 1939, Finland was invaded by the Soviet Union.  The
Finns, although vastly outnumbered, were determined to defend their
country.  The Soviet High Command hoped to "cut Finland in two" by
driving past the key road junction of Suomussalmi and continuing to the
Baltic Sea.  The Finnish commander, von Mannerheim, believed the
Soviet attack had to be stopped at Suomussalmi, or his nation was
doomed.
The Finnish forces have trapped one Soviet division in and around
Suomussalmi, but an even more powerful Soviet relief force is moving to
their aid.
Commander, you have delayed the enemy long enough to allow our evacuation at Dunkirk. We cannot afford to keep taking such losses. We expect much more from you.

Commander, once again the Americans need our help. The Germans have launched a major counterattack in the Ardennes region. The Americans have been forced to retreat. You will take command of all allied forces in the region and drive the Germans back.
Commander, you did a good job. We can continue our offensive towards the German border.
Good job, Commander. Your success has allowed British troops to pour into southern Italy.  And, as we surmised, Italy may be on the verge of surrendering.
The offensive has not gone as well as we hoped. In your sector, at least, you have not even managed to control the passes!
If it was not for the Americans you would have failed completely, this is not a performance we expected of you - unfortunately I will have to remove you from your command.

The war effort has come to a critical junction, Commander.  Now that British and Commonwealth troops have landed on the beaches of Normandy, we must surge ahead.  The big push will come at St. Lo, where Jerry is well entrenched.  You must force him back and drive through his lines.  If you cannot achieve some level of success quickly,  the Germans could well give us a hard time in this hedgerow country forever!  Press on.

Splendid job, Commander. Quite splendid.  Due to your, if I do say so myself, splendid performance at St. Lo, our forces will have the impetus they require to break out of Normandy and liberate France.  But now your services are needed at Caen, where Monty is having a spot of bother with Jerry.

Back from your mission, Commander?  Good. I must say, you were rather long about it.  At least, you took your objectives, I'll grant you that.  But now, your presence is needed at Caen, where the Germans are delaying our advance.  Hopefully,  you will improve your performance.

Well, Commander, you are to be given not only a promotion, but also an audience with the Duke of Penzance. It is very important to portray a picture of  success and, thanks to your failure, this will be extremely difficult.  Good day, Commander.  We will not meet again.

Well, Commander, our invasion of Normandy has bogged down near Caen.  Do you know Caen was home to William the Conqueror, 1066 and all that?   At any rate, Commonwealth forces must drive through Caen and press on into France.

Caen proved to be a sticky wicket, indeed, but you brought us off the pitch with no trouble at all.  It was a difficult area for our brave men to break through, but you did it!  By jove, you did it. Good work!  Now, our lads are on their way to liberate all of France.

Well,  you had a spot of trouble while capturing Caen.  Nevertheless, British pluck won out in the end. However, the battle of Caen will soon be forgotten as other more glorious victories are won.  Onward, Commander.

Well, Commander, I would offer you tea, but after your disappointing performance, it would be difficult to have you in the vicinity without choking on my crumpet.  There's talk at GHQ of your relief.  It seems to be the most positive solution under the circumstances.

Your mission is to capture the important industrial city of Nancy and secure a springboard for our fall offensive into Germany itself. Without full control of this rail and shipping center, our advance will be impossible.  Commander, please be advised, that directly east of the city, Jerry has armored forces ready to counterattack any offensive against this stronghold.

Well, it appears you did manage to take the city, but it seems that, this is all you managed to do.  The enemy has withdrawn and regrouped, and now await us some 20 miles down the road.  Another indifferent performance like this one and the Yanks will be claiming they are winning the war!

I must say, I do find it hard to believe that you secured a King's commission.  I believe promotion by purchase was banned in the last century. Your name, sir, shall be stricken from your regiment's otherwise honorable rolls.  Your services will no longer be required.

I would invite you to tea Commander, but, there is simply no time.  My apologies.  Here is the situation. The Germans have held the fortress city of Metz for two months against American attacks, and now the Yanks have requested our help.  Our troops must  smash Jerry's resistance, then punch through the Maginot Line. Metz is the site of the German training schools for officers and NCOs, so you can expect a tough fight.  This mission is crucial, Commander.  You must act decisively.

Congratulations! Your troops stormed the city in a charge that Henry V would admire!  Your victory at Metz shall stand alongside the great battles of Agincourt and Cressy.  I have heard your name mentioned several times in relation to some promotion or advancement.  Commander, your successful offensive has paved the way to our invasion of the "fatherland."
That performance makes m e think you're auditioning for a command in
the Pacific.
Well done.

Well, what can I say?  You did manage to secure your objectives as well as capture a few Jerries.  A comparatively successful performance, and the war has been won.

American and British troops are to land at Salerno and begin a Second Front against the Germans and knock Italy out of the war.  Once you're ashore, you'll need to get your men off those beaches  pronto.  By the way, you should be aware that the Krauts have got a panzer division somewhere in the area.  Good luck, Commander.
